Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the draft MSA+Order Form and returned a set of redlines focused on uptime and credits. High-level asks:

- Move uptime commitment to 99.99% (current draft: 99.95%).
- Expand service credit tiers to 20% for monthly availability <99.75% and 50% for <99.5%.
- Remove the clause that allows Redwood to schedule maintenance with only 48 hours' notice; Kestrel requires a 7-day notice window and a one-hour emergency rollback SLA.
- Tighten P1/P2 response times to 30/120 minutes respectively (we understand your current ops page lists 60/240).

We attached the marked Order Form (Kestrel_Redlines_OrderForm_20281127.pdf). Can you confirm what you can accept and what needs escalation to legal/leadership? We need to close procurement by mid-December.

Appreciate a line-by-line if possible.

—Ellie

Thanks Ellie — useful and clear.

Short answer up front: we can accept a compromise on a higher availability target and tighter response windows with adjusted credit caps and tighter maintenance definitions. We'll need a short legal review for exact wording on credits and emergency maintenance carveouts (looping in Lauren and Soojin).

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Redwood proposes a target commitment of 99.95% in the Order Form with a separate negotiated Appendix that allows an elevated 99.99% target for an additional SLA uplift (one-time setup and 10% monthly uplift). If Kestrel wants 99.99 now, we can price and commit to it under a dedicated capacity addendum.
- Reduce maximum credit exposure: agree to tiered credits but cap cumulative credits per 12-month period at 100% of one month’s fees.
- Define Maintenance: standard maintenance = weekly rolling windows (2 x 4-hour windows per month) with 7 days' notice; emergency maintenance = immediate actions limited to P0 incidents only, with rollback windows and an internal postmortem commitment within 72 hours.
- Response SLOs: suggest 60/180 minutes (P1/P2) as baseline; we can accept 30/120 for customers on dedicated capacity or higher support tiers.

If these principles look workable, legal will produce redline language and we'll return a clean Order Form and an optional SLA Amendment for dedicated capacity. We can aim to finalize redlines by Thu, 2028-11-30 to keep procurement timelines intact.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow to align on the uplift vs credit tradeoffs?

Best,

Team — forwarding Ellie’s redlines (below). Need quick legal take:

Quoted from Ellie: "Move uptime commitment to 99.99% ... Expand service credit tiers to 20% for monthly availability <99.75% and 50% for <99.5% ... require 7-day notice for maintenance ... P1/P2 response times 30/120 minutes."

Questions for legal / ops:
- Credit exposure: if we accept their tiers, cumulative credit risk spikes. Recommend we limit cumulative credits to one-month fees per rolling 12 months and cap any single-month credit to 25% unless on dedicated capacity. Thoughts?
- Emergency maintenance carveout: they want rollback SLA and 7-day notice for regular maintenance. Ops can define emergency scopes; should legal insist on wording that limits "emergency maintenance" to actions necessary to prevent material harm / imminent security risk?
- Response times: are the tightened times acceptable only for dedicated customers or can we offer a commercial SLA clause that says "response times as specified for customers on an enhanced support plan"?

Karthik — please flag if pricing uplift is possible for a 99.99 commitment (we need numbers). Lauren/Soojin — could you draft two short redline options (safe/legal-preserving + commercial-compromise) I can send back to Ellie? Procurement wants closure mid-December.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa / team / Kestrel —

Thanks for laying out the asks. Below are concise, negotiable redline suggestions we can share now. Drafted to protect Redwood’s exposure while giving Kestrel commercial levers. Please read as (A) baseline (what we accept in the Order Form) and (B) optional upgrade (separate SLA Amendment/dedicated capacity).

1) Availability Commitment
- Baseline: "Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Service available 99.95% of the time in a monthly billing cycle. Service credits for Availability are tiered as follows: Monthly availability <99.95% and >=99.5% — 10% credit; <99.5% and >=99.0% — 25% credit; <99.0% — 50% credit. Cumulative credit liability is capped at 100% of one month’s Subscription Fees in any 12-month rolling period."
- Optional Upgrade: "99.99% availability commitment available by execution of an SLA Amendment and a 10% monthly fee uplift or a one-time implementation fee as agreed in the Order Form."

2) Maintenance / Exclusions
- "Provider may schedule non-emergency maintenance during published maintenance windows (maximum two 4-hour windows per calendar month) with at least 7 days' advance notice. Emergency maintenance may be performed without 7 days' notice where required to mitigate a security incident or imminent material harm; Provider shall use reasonable efforts to notify Customer as soon as practicable and shall provide a post-incident report within 72 hours of remediation."
- Include explicit definition of "Emergency Maintenance" limited to security incidents, P0 system integrity issues, or mandated regulatory patches.

3) Response Times and Escalation
- Baseline Response SLOs: P1: acknowledge within 60 minutes, P2: acknowledge within 180 minutes.
- Enhanced Support: 30/120 acknowledgement windows available for customers that execute the Enhanced Support Addendum or are on dedicated capacity.

4) Credits Calculation and Remedy Limitations
- Credits will be the sole and exclusive remedy for Availability failures and are applied to the next invoice. Except for willful misconduct or gross negligence, Provider’s aggregate liability for Availability credits is limited to the cap described above.

Next steps: Lauren / I will prepare two tracked-redline documents: (1) commercial compromise for immediate exchange with Kestrel; (2) legal-preserving redline if Kestrel insists on 99.99 without uplift. I’ll attach both and a suggested email to close. Marissa — if Kestrel accepts baseline + upgrade path, I’m ok moving forward without exec escalation. If they insist on 99.99 with unlimited credits, escalate to Sarah/CTO (we should avoid that).

I'll attach the two redline docs in the next hour and include a DocuSign-ready Order Form if they accept.

—Soojin
